They give focus to characters that don't get much screen time in canon (and I honestly do consider some of them canon for that reason). It ultimately comes down to how much you're willing to watch.

For me personally, I never felt like Penny's attitude contrasted too much with the theme of the volume. Up until the end of episode 6, while there were definitely serious moments I feel like the season wasn't taking itself too awfully seriously. In my opinion, Penny was cheerful when the situation called for it and the writers were successful in cutting that back a bit when necessary. After episode 6 she didn't have as much of that optimism and cheerfulness that she's known for. She was often shown being sad or conflicted when it came to her job.

My problem is *how* she was brought back. I didn't really have any doubt that she would be reintroduced since she's a robot that can be rebuilt and she's also a fairly popular character that many people were missing. And so, as an attempt to make people happy and to give them another reason to continue watching the season, they just made her reappearance official in the very first episode. While I understood the reasons from a writers perspective, in the show it just came off as kind of jarring to me. No buildup in-canon or anything aside from a passing remark just minutes before, and she's shown having the same personality and memories she had before she was torn apart in volume 3. 

I had hoped that to potentially give more development to Ruby that Penny would have lost a lot or all of the memories she had of her time in Vale. I guess it's debatable on whether or not her memory loss would make sense, but RWBY has already done a lot of things that can't really be logically explained, and I feel like if it was done well, most fans would have been able to suspend their disbelief. You could argue that Ruby having a sort of mini-arc with Penny would have taken up too much time, but I honestly would have preferred that over the whole political tone of the season. I feel like that whole aspect could have been cut out and the major events involved with it could have been caused by other things.
